# Section II - What makes Synergy Different

Most of the time, you should be able to look at an ability, a piece of gear, or a spell and have a good sense of what it does and how it might be used. The system gets out of the way so the city can do its job.

Rather than limiting what players can attempt, Shadows focuses on how the world responds. You’re encouraged to take bold actions, try unexpected solutions, and push your Luck. The rules aren’t there to stop you - they’re there to make sure the consequences matter.

This is **Synergy**. The parts move together. When they do, the mechanics stop being visible and the fiction takes over.

Whether you're counting every modifier or just rolling and reacting, the system holds up. It was built to.

## Story through uncertainty

When someone tells a story around a campfire, nothing stops them from polishing the details or choosing the ending they like best. Tabletop roleplaying works differently. In Shadows, the story belongs to everyone at the table, and no one gets to decide how it turns out alone.

You’re free to attempt almost anything. Talk your way past a guard. Intimidate a fixer. Run headlong into danger with a bad plan and a worse backup. What you aren’t guaranteed is success. When the outcome of an action is uncertain, the GM may ask you to see how it plays out. These moments aren’t interruptions. They’re where the story happens, where tension lives, where plans bend, and where characters reveal who they really are once things stop going according to script.

Maybe you try to strong-arm a shop owner who’s already tired of being threatened. The attempt doesn’t go the way you hoped. Now the room is colder. The price just went up. Or maybe you’ve made an enemy who won’t forget your face. The story doesn’t stop…it *turns*. And now you’re in new trouble.

Shadows is built around responding to these turns. Success feels earned because it isn’t automatic. Failure doesn’t end the scene; it creates new problems to solve. When an action does not go the way you planned, always be asking: **What do you do next?**

This is how stories in NYTE City are shaped. Not by perfect plans, but by imperfect choices made under pressure, in a world that remembers what you try.

## The Core of Synergy

NYTE City is unforgiving. Your character is defined by a set of character traits that measure how you think, move, endure, and connect in a world that actively pushes back. These traits don’t tell you who you are, they tell the city how hard it must hit before you break. These traits are categorized as:

- Stats

- Attributes

- Skills

### Stats

**Stats** describe how your body and mind function when things go wrong. They govern movement, violence, stress, technology, and human connection; the fundamentals of surviving another night in NYTE City. Basic Stats are rated on a scale that reflects how capable you are compared to an ordinary human living in NYTE City. Most people fall somewhere in the middle (4-6). Drop too far below that, and the world starts pushing back harder. Rise above it, and doors begin to open…sometimes dangerous ones.

Here are some Stat ranges at a glance:

- **3 or lower** means you’re either very young or old, you’ve got some old injury or trauma, poor genetics, or hard living has left a mark. This will matter in play.

- **4–6** is human average. You get by. You don’t stand out.

- **7–9** means you’re exceptional. The city notices.

- **10** is the edge of human potential. Pushing past this comes at a cost.

Stats below average make actions harder and introduce complications more often. High stats make success more reliable but never guaranteed. **Every point you move away from average matters.**

Sidebar: **Beyond Human Limits**

Some Archetypes, like Vampires and Werewolves, are not bound by normal human ceilings. Their Basic Stats can exceed 10, representing centuries of experience, inhuman physiology, or supernatural power.

That kind of strength doesn’t scale the same way. Once a stat passes 10, gains slow down. You’re not getting stronger the way a human does; you’re stretching the limits of reality instead.

The exact mechanics for this are explained later. For now, understand this: **supernatural power is real, but it’s never free.**

- Body (BOD)

> BOD is the machine you were issued at birth. It sets how much punishment you absorb before the city wins: your Health, your endurance, what you can lift, how much pain you can carry without folding, and whether poison and infection take hold or get turned away. When you swing a blade or throw a punch, BOD sets the baseline damage.

- Reflexes (REF)

Hand-eye coordination, agility, raw reaction speed, and accuracy with weapons. Used heavily in combat, spellcasting under pressure, and any moment where hesitation gets you killed.

- Mobility (MOB)

> MOB is how fast you move when staying put stops being an option. It sets your running speed, your sprint, and how far a running start carries you.

- **Intelligence (INT)**

> INT is the edge that cuts through noise. Pattern recognition, argumentation, the ability to think three moves ahead when everyone else is still reacting.

- Technological Aptitude (TECH)

TECH measures how well you understand the machines that run the city - and how badly things go when you don’t. It governs your ability to use, break, modify, or survive technology that was never designed with your safety in mind.

- **Cool (COOL)**

COOL is how you act when everything is on the line and everyone is watching. Panic is contagious. So is confidence. COOL decides which one you bring into the room.

- Magnetism (MAG)

MAG is presence. The way a room shifts when you walk in. People trust you, follow you, and sometimes don’t know why. That’s not charm – that’s gravity.

- Empathy (EMP)

Empathy stands alone as the emotional and intuitive Stat. It has direct correlation to your Sanity and is a snapshot of your character's overall humanity. Low EMP leaves people cold to themselves and colder to others. It is also the first thing NYTE City takes.

### Attributes

These attributes are the more ethereal side of your character and are derived from your Stats. Attributes represent how your character pushes back against the pressures of NYTE City. If there’s a thread running through these attributes, it’s Empathy (EMP). EMP is the measure of how long you can keep going before NYTE City takes something from you.

**Tolerance** (TOL)

**TOL** measures how much strain your body can endure before the power you wield starts pushing back. Whether you’re channeling Aether through your body or running cybernetics that feed on your bioelectricity, there is a limit and crossing it has consequences.

As you cast spells or activate cybernetics, **Exhaustion** builds. Push too far, and your body refuses to cooperate: spells fizzle, systems fail, and the moment slips through your fingers.

**TOL** is based on your **INT**, **COOL**, and **EMP** bonuses.

**Will** **(WILL)**

Will is your defense against intrusion - mental, emotional, or supernatural. It comes into play when something tries to break you from the inside, whether through psychic force, manipulation, or temptation dressed up as an easy way out.

Your WILL is based on your **BODY**, **INT**, and **EMP** bonuses.

**Sanity** **(SAN)**

Everyone learns to live with NYTE City in their own way. The violence, the rituals, the things you’re expected to accept as normal; it all takes its toll. In Shadows, no one is completely sane.

SAN comes into play when you encounter something that threatens to fracture your grasp on reality. As it drops, the world becomes colder, crueler, and harder to make sense of.

Sanity is your connection to reality and its people. It is based on your **EMP** stat alone.

### Skills

Skills represent what your character has learned or trained in over the course of their life. Experience earned the hard way, habits formed under pressure, and competence paid for in scars. They aren’t your only path to success, but they shape how you get there.

Every skill is tied to two basic stats: **a primary stat** and a **Synergy bonus**. The Primary Stat reflects your instinctive aptitude, while the Synergy Bonus represents the trait that sharpens, contextualized, or supports that instinct.

Even without formal training, raw capability matters. Strong stats can carry you through unfamiliar situations; training only refines that edge.

This is Synergy in practice. Preparation helps. Instinct matters. No single number tells the whole story.

The world has its shape. Its streets, its monsters, its pressure, and the kind of person your character has become just to survive in it. Now the mechanics catch up to the fiction.
